page: Vultr vx1-m-4c-32gb is a memory-optimized server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. Memory capacity stands at 32.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is limited to 1 GB of network-attached storage, and no GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-threaded performance alongside average multi-threaded capabilities. The server achieves top-tier status in single-core stress-ng CPU tests and single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 25%, and multi-core stress-ng CPU performance sits in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth is average, with read-only small block cached speeds at 440.83 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 41.08 GB/sec.

The server exhibits a clear tradeoff between its high memory allocation and its moderate multi-core processing capabilities. While single-threaded execution is highly efficient, intensive multi-threaded workloads and complex LLM prompt processing on medium models are bottlenecked by the 4-vCPU limit. This profile is suitable for memory-intensive but compute-moderate workloads, such as database operations, Redis caching, and static web serving.
